changelog: **External Correction — Robust tracking mode** (`corrMode = 4`, now the default): a decoupled proprioceptive servo replaces the measurement-gated EMA. A constant-velocity estimate is predicted every 1-ms tick and corrected on each frame, so the correction stays alive through dropped or irregular frames instead of collapsing between them. Sensor latency is compensated via the frame-age field (measurement extrapolated to "now"). Four tuning sliders: **Tracking α** (measurement trust), **Snap KP** (pull strength, 1 % steps), **Lead KD** (velocity feed-forward for moving targets), **Switch-Margin** (center-bias for object switching). Uses the existing Object-Gate / Switch-Frames / Correction Box / Max-Step controls.

**External Correction — Snap mode** (`corrMode = 3`): discrete jumps onto the target at a fixed interval (**Snapping idle time**), each distributed over a **Corr. Time** in 1-ms sub-steps. The user's own mouse movement is suppressed during the correction window (buttons/clicks pass through).
**External Correction — RMB trigger**: the activation gate is now three-way — **Always** / **only while LMB held** / **only while RMB held**.
**External Correction — Correction Box (X / Y)**: a box of the given pixel size around the screen centre; if the target lies outside the box the correction is fully ignored (all modes). 0 = axis off.

**External Correction — global MIM-spline switch**: the "Add. MIM/CIM Splines" toggle now governs the MIM velocity-spline unconditionally, independent of whether external correction is enabled — unchecked = spline never runs. Default is now ON so plain MIM works out of the box.

**Robust mode instability** — above ~10 % Snap KP the corrector overshot out of the box and froze. The α-β velocity estimate was contaminated by the corrector's own actuation (positive feedback), and the resulting jump pushed the target outside the box gate, which then blocked all further correction. Reworked to a servo where the own motion is dead-reckoned out of the estimate; KP is now stable up to 100 %.

**Robust mode — Object-Gate froze the corrector** — with Object-Gate > 0 the correction stopped moving. The tracker's internal gate compared the fresh measurement against the dead-reckoned estimate, which a working correction deliberately drives apart, so the real target was misclassified as a rival. Robust mode now routes through the shared object gate (raw-measurement space, scale-independent).

**Snap mode — user-mouse lockup** — a running snap window that exited via an early return (LMB/RMB released, deadband, signal lost, priority-gain 0) left the user's mouse motion permanently suppressed. Every early return now cancels the snap window.
